title: Controlling Vision-Language Models for Multi-Task Image Restoration
layout_note: Left two thirds: training. A frozen text encoder (top) and frozen image encoder (middle) sit in one light-blue dashed 'Pretrained CLIP' frame, a trainable image controller sits below; their four embeddings form two text-over-image pairs around one grey 'Contrastive Learning' bar. Right third: the trained DA-CLIP drawn small (encoder over controller) feeding a red diffusion restoration block between an LQ photo above and an HQ photo below. A dashed legend box along the bottom names the four embeddings.
grouping: A light-blue dashed rounded frame groups the two frozen CLIP encoders (labelled 'Pretrained CLIP'); a second, smaller light-blue dashed frame labelled 'DA-CLIP' groups the encoder and controller in the right panel; the contrastive objective is a grey dashed pill; the legend is a full-width grey dashed box at the bottom. Colour families tie each embedding bar to the module that makes it.
shapes_depth: Encoders and the controller are flat trapezoids (purple text encoder, green image encoder, yellow controller) with a small padlock icon (blue closed = frozen, red open = trainable); embeddings are flat stacked bars in the maker's colour; inputs are a stacked word card ('snowy'), a stacked caption card and a stacked real photo; the restoration model is a red rounded rectangle with a small bow-tie U-Net glyph and an open red padlock.
proposed_highlight: The new image controller is the only yellow module and carries a red open padlock against the blue closed padlocks of the frozen CLIP encoders; its degradation embedding is a yellow bar, and purple dashed 'gradient flow' arrows show that only the controller is trained.
lesson: Colour each embedding bar with the colour of the module that makes it and stack the text-side bar over the image-side bar with one objective bar between them, so the two contrastive pairs read by position and colour before any label.
notes: venue verified from the PDF header ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024'). Method name DA-CLIP from the caption. Fig. 3 of the paper opens the controller (zero-dense connections into the encoder's transformer blocks) and the prompt module.

arrangement.units: unframed training panel (left, about two thirds of the width) and an unframed usage panel (right) holding a small dashed-framed DA-CLIP unit; a dashed legend strip spans the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text cards ('snowy', 'seagull sitting on a post') and a real degraded photo at the left of the training panel; the usage panel takes a real LQ photo from its top right and puts the restored HQ photo below
arrangement.losses_at: one grey 'Contrastive Learning' bar in the middle of the training panel, between the text-side embeddings above and the image-side embeddings below
arrangement.shared: the image encoder appears in both panels; in the training panel the controller receives a 'copy' of it and sends 'control' back, drawn as two short vertical arrows

taxonomy.task: multi-task image restoration steered by degradation embeddings from a controlled CLIP

insights.structure: Text encoder over image encoder over controller form a left column; their four embedding bars sit to the right in a two-by-two block (text row above, image row below) around one Contrastive Learning bar; the deployed model sits in a separate right panel.
insights.data: Inputs are drawn as data (a stacked degradation word card, a stacked caption card, a real snowy photo), and every embedding is a stacked bar named with a symbol (e_c^T, e_d^T, e_c^I, e_d^I) that the bottom legend spells out.
insights.emphasis: The trainable controller is the only yellow module and the only red open padlock among the encoders; purple dashed gradient-flow arrows run only into the controller.
insights.flow: Thin black orthogonal arrows run left to right from inputs to encoders to embeddings and up or down into the objective; the gradient-flow arrows are dashed purple and run back along the bottom and up the encoder column; the right panel reads top to bottom from LQ to HQ.
insights.avoid: The degradation embedding e_d^I is wired to the controller by a long dashed gradient line that runs along the bottom of the panel, and the right panel repeats the encoder and controller at a much smaller scale without a visible link to the left one.

core.what: two text-side embeddings (caption e_c^T, degradation e_d^T) above and two image-side embeddings (content e_c^I, degradation e_d^I) below face each other across one grey Contrastive Learning bar

relations.form: the two contrastive pairs stand as two columns, each a purple text bar over a green or yellow image bar, with the shared objective bar running between the rows
one Contrastive Learning bar spans both pairs, with an arrow down from each text bar and up from each image bar
the controller sits directly under the image encoder; a 'copy' arrow runs down and a 'control' arrow runs up between them, both short and vertical
training on the left, deployment on the right: the trained DA-CLIP is redrawn small and its two embeddings enter the red restoration block from the left as 'Cross Attention' and 'Prompt'
in the right panel the green content embedding and the yellow degradation embedding converge on the red diffusion block from its left side by two short curved arrows

channels.colour: purple = text-side (text encoder and its embeddings), green = image encoder and its content embedding, yellow = controller and its degradation embedding, red = the downstream restoration model; padlock colour = frozen (blue closed) vs trainable (red open); purple is also used for the dashed gradient-flow arrows, a second meaning for that hue
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder or controller, flat stacked bar = embedding, stacked card = text input, photo = image input, pill = objective, rounded rectangle = restoration model
channels.line: solid black = forward data flow; dashed purple = gradient flow (training only)
channels.frame: dashed light-blue rounded frame = one pretrained model (Pretrained CLIP, DA-CLIP); dashed grey = objective and legend

quality.strengths: Each embedding is drawn as a coloured bar between the encoder that makes it and the contrastive bar that compares it, so what is compared with what is visible from position and colour; frozen vs trainable is carried by one icon channel (padlock colour) rather than fill; the gradient-flow line style marks training-only paths; inputs are real data (a word card, a caption, a degraded photo).
quality.weaknesses: Purple marks both the text side and the gradient-flow arrows; the long dashed gradient line from e_d^I runs along the bottom and turns up into the controller; the deployment panel redraws DA-CLIP at about a quarter of the size with no tie to the training panel beyond the shared colours; the 'degradation type' output of the text encoder runs as a long elbow over the caption wire to reach e_d^T.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
